t.E585.agn: In 1989 JECFA included ferrous lactate in the provisional maximum tolerable daily intake (PMTDI) of 0.8 mg/kg body weight/day, expressed as iron (Fe) and applying to all sources of iron; no separate toxicological monograph was prepared. In the EU it is authorised only in darkened olives and one species of mushroom; EFSA issued a call for data for its re-evaluation in 2012, and there is no finalised opinion yet.
t.E585.body: Enters the body as iron and lactate.
t.E585.found.0: Black olives darkened by oxidation (in the EU max. 150 mg/kg, as iron)
t.E585.found.1: Albatrellus ovinus mushroom used in Swedish-style liver pâtés (in the EU, this use only)
t.E585.prod: Obtained by reacting lactic acid or lactate salts with iron compounds; lactic acid may be produced by fermentation or by chemical synthesis.
t.E585.regx.0: Group PMTDI for iron 0.8 mg/kg body weight/day (as Fe).
t.E585.regx.1: Only in olives darkened by oxidation and in Albatrellus ovinus mushroom in Swedish liver pâtés, max. 150 mg/kg (as Fe).
t.E585.regx.2: Included in the call for scientific data for re-evaluation (deadline 01.01.2013).
t.E585.summary: The iron salt of lactic acid. Stabilises the colour of black olives.
t.E585.what: An iron salt used to stabilise the black colour of olives darkened by oxidation (colour stabiliser).
